title: Interactive SIR/SEIR Epidemic Simulator
description: Solves the SIR, SEIR, SEIRD, and SEIRV compartmental epidemic models over 365 days. Sliders set the transmission, recovery, progression, mortality, and vaccination rates and the population size. The charts show each compartment, the herd immunity threshold, the overshoot, and cumulative cases and deaths. A Compare button overlays a saved run.

learning_objective: Apply the SIR and SEIR family of models by changing their parameters to predict how R0, the epidemic peak, the total infected, and the overshoot past the herd immunity threshold respond.

learningObjectives: Compute R0 and the herd immunity threshold from beta and gamma
Predict how the epidemic peak and total infected change when a parameter changes
Compare the SIR, SEIR, SEIRD, and SEIRV models

controls.label: Save Run to Compare / Clear Saved Run
controls.description: Keeps the current run on the charts as dashed lines.

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Restores the default model and parameters.

equations: dI/dt = sigma*E - gamma*I  (SIR: beta*S*I/N - gamma*I; SEIRD: - (gamma + mu)*I)
assumptions: Permanent immunity after recovery or vaccination
Constant parameters for the whole run
0.1% of the population is infectious on day 0
limitations: No births, natural deaths, or waning immunity
No age structure, contact networks, or behavior change
Parameters cannot change in the middle of a run

keyQuestions: Why does the epidemic infect more people than the herd immunity threshold?
Why does lowering beta reduce total infections and not only the peak?
Which outputs change when a latent period is added?
commonMisconceptions: The epidemic stops as soon as the herd immunity threshold is reached
Flattening the curve only delays cases and does not prevent them
A longer latent period changes R0
assessmentOpportunities: Compute R0 and the herd immunity threshold from beta and gamma
